author: BBC News
description:
Pope Leo XIV's recovery from surgery to remove a lower lobe of his lung is "progressing as expected", his doctors have said.
 
The 71-year-old pontiff has started to walk and has "resumed a normal diet" following the roughly 90-minute procedure, the medics said in an update shared by the Vatican.
 
The Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.
 
Blood tests and an X-ray early on Wednesday showed his recovery was "proceeding normally", the doctors said, and he has also undergone respiratory physiotherapy.
 
The pontiff is expected to remain there for about a week as he recovers.

description:
This week tens of thousands of young people have taken to the streets of Delhi, India’s capital, demanding changes to the electoral system and the resignation of the country’s electoral commissioner. Thousands have been detained by police in the process.

They represent the ‘cockroach’ movement, a grassroots campaign group started by a Boston University graduate in protest at government policies and high youth unemployment. How did a movement that started as a meme capture the minds of India’s young people, and start to pose a challenge to its long-serving prime minister, Narendra Modi?

The BBC’s South Asia correspondent, Azadeh Moshiri, explains.

Russell Brand was described as "ruthless" and a "sexual predator" by the prosecution at the start of his trial for rape and sexual assault on Wednesday.
 
The 51-year-old actor and comedian faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.
 
Riel Karmy-Jones KC, for the prosecution, told Southwark Crown Court in London the women "did not know each other", "have never met each other" and "came forward independently of each other".

Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed.

author: BBC News
description:
The Vatican has confirmed that Pope Leo XIV had a ‘peaceful night’ in hospital after surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung on Tuesday.
 
The pontiff is expected to remain in Rome's Gemelli Hospital for about a week before returning to work.
 
The 71-year-old underwent a 90-minute surgery on Tuesday and was subsequently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer.
 
Leo had announced his surgery to a crowd in St Peter’s Square on Sunday, telling them doctors had found a nodule on his lung.
 
Although nodules are quite common and often benign, the Vatican said that a pre-operative examination of Pope Leo’s suggested it to be cancerous.
 
Cardinal Kikuchi Tarcisio Isao of Tokyo said he met with Leo on Monday and that Leo explained he felt physically fine, and had opted for the surgery as soon as possible so as not to delay a planned trip to Latin America in early November.

At least 600,000 people in Ukraine are without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
 
For the second night, Ukraine received no early warning from its partners that an attack was imminent, he added.
 
At least six people were killed in the strikes, and 21 injured, and officials said that access to the Starlink communications system was restricted overnight.
 
The attacks come after US President Donald Trump's claim on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine.
